bank_plan.formula: (lesson_check_items + module_check_items) x 2 alternates + forms x form_length
bank_plan.eighty_twenty_note: 80% instruction / 20% assessment honoured at course level (I+A=T); bank serves lesson checks, module checks, 3 practice forms and a protected final.
bank_plan.size_band_note: Planning range per assessment standard (200-600 skills; 600-1500+ large certification). This is a planning guide, not proof of quality.

mcq_limitation_note: NCLEX includes alternate and next-generation clinical-judgment item formats; Mastemy uses MCQ/MR only and does not replicate clinical performance.

items.stem: A nurse is assigned four patients at the start of a shift. Which patient should be assessed first?

options.text: A post-operative patient reporting sudden shortness of breath
options.rationale: Correct: a potential airway/breathing emergency takes priority over stable needs.

options.text: A patient requesting pain medication for chronic back pain
options.rationale: Important but not immediately life-threatening compared with acute dyspnoea.
Discharge teaching is not time-critical relative to an acute change.

options.text: A patient asking for help with a meal tray
options.rationale: A comfort need, lowest priority among these options.

items.explanation: Airway and breathing problems are prioritised using the ABC framework.
items.provenance: AI-drafted original item, not from any proprietary, leaked or paid exam source

items.stem: Which precaution is required for a patient with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis?

options.text: Airborne precautions with a fit-tested respirator and negative-pressure room
options.rationale: Correct: TB spreads via airborne droplet nuclei, requiring airborne precautions.

options.text: Contact precautions with gown and gloves only
options.rationale: Contact precautions do not protect against airborne transmission.

options.text: Droplet precautions with a surgical mask only
options.rationale: Droplet precautions are insufficient for airborne pathogens like TB.
Standard precautions do not address airborne transmission.

items.explanation: Pulmonary TB requires airborne precautions, a respirator and a negative-pressure room.
items.provenance: AI-drafted original item, not from any proprietary, leaked or paid exam source

items.stem: Which TWO actions are required before administering a high-alert medication?

options.text: Verify the dose against a weight-based or protocol calculation
options.rationale: Correct: independent dose verification reduces high-alert medication errors.

options.text: Complete an independent double-check with a second nurse where policy requires
options.rationale: Correct: independent double-checks are a standard high-alert safeguard.

options.text: Administer first and document the order afterward
options.rationale: Giving a medication before confirming the order is unsafe.

options.text: Skip identity checks if the patient is familiar
Round the dose up to the nearest convenient amount
options.rationale: Altering a calculated dose for convenience is unsafe.

items.explanation: High-alert medications require dose verification and, where policy dictates, an independent double-check.
